notes.title: Werewolf: The Apocalypse — Purgatory is Out Now!
notes.content:
[h2]Hello, renegades![/h2]

We're excited to share that our friends' new title, [b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2463980/Werewolf_The_Apocalypse__Purgatory/]Werewolf: The Apocalypse — Purgatory[/url], is out now![/b]

Follow Samira, an Afghan werewolf and refugee, as she navigates both supernatural and human challenges in her quest for survival.

[h3]🐺 About Werewolf The Apocalypse – Purgatory:[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]A new perspective[/b] – explore Samira's inner conflicts through a story-rich roleplaying game as she battles between rage and despair as an Afghan werewolf and refugee.
[*] [b]Thrilling conspiracies[/b] – uncover the supernatural secrets of the werewolves’ world through two distinct story paths, each offering different challenges and consequences.
[*] [b]Be the werewolf[/b] – intimidate, manipulate or when all else fails, decimate all that stands in your way.
[*] [b]Tabletop RPG meets visual novel[/b] – experience a blend of narrative-driven gameplay and tabletop RPG mechanics.
[*] [b]Legendary World of Darkness lore[/b] – based on the new fifth edition corebook mechanics, the game emulates a classic role-playing experience.
[/list]
[previewyoutube=TaEmz3Xkui4;full][/previewyoutube]
This edition not only continues the rich narrative tradition of its predecessors but also incorporates the innovative features of the [b]Werewolf: The Apocalypse Fifth Edition[/b]. This adaptation enhances gameplay, deepening your engagement with the lore and mechanics.

Whether you’re struggling against despair or raging against fate, your choices will carve Samira’s path through the game. Uncover supernatural conspiracies, battle the chaotic forces of the [i]Wyrm[/i], and navigate the haunting streets of Warsaw.

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2463980/Werewolf_The_Apocalypse__Purgatory/]Werewolf: The Apocalypse — Purgatory[/url] welcomes both seasoned World of Darkness veterans and newcomers alike. [b]No prior knowledge of the story world or Werewolf: The Apocalypse — Heart of the Forest is needed.[/b] The game includes familiar characters and settings, enhanced with helpful pop-ups for new vocabulary that offer pronunciation tips, definitions, and lore to deepen your immersion.

We hope you'll enjoy the story!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2463980/Werewolf_The_Apocalypse__Purgatory/

notes.title: Check out HAVENDOCK - become the creator of a colony in the middle of the ocean!
notes.content:
Hi there!

Our friends at[url=https://store.steampowered.com/publisher/DifferentTales] Different Tales[/url] published a very cozy sim about building a colony from scratch in the middle of the ocean. It’s [b]a great way to spend a relaxing weekend[/b] - you know, with a cold drink during a sunny day or a hot beverage during a cold night and building and tweaking your dreamed design of a haven. 

See the trailer: 
[previewyoutube=WGQOr9BhH30;full][/previewyoutube]
In Havendock you can [b]create your own character[/b], collect resources, build facilities and farms, arrange your settlement, raise and feed animals, as well as welcome new survivors. 
You will need to[b] manage your tasks and production[/b] to keep everyone[b] happy and healthy[/b], but don't worry - everything is super cozy and easy to learn - especially when playing with friends! 

Havendock also let's you play in [b]co-op[/b] as part of its experimental multiplayer mode, and the e[b]ntire game will be growing in quality and size[/b] alongside its early access development plans.

notes.title: Werewolf: The Apocalypse — Heart of the Forest 1st Anniversary!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38367964/ee6a9a7c385b8335e12c40751078b4d5acaa70a6.jpg[/img]

[b]Exactly one year ago, we've released the very first Werewolf: The Apocalypse video game in history! [/b]

Now - one year later, we can honestly say that we couldn't be happier about the influence the game created. Not only did the Different Tales team [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1342620/view/3048342819249943399]won one of the most important cultural awards in Poland -  Paszporty Polityki[/url], as well as [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1342620/view/2947004218185020375]the Best Game Design Award at the Dev.Play 2020 Digital Awards[/url], but the game gained such a great reaction and feedback from you - the players, which we couldn't even imagine.
[previewyoutube=rbcWM3N2mM8;full][/previewyoutube]

The project itself was super important and personal for the Different Tales team, as the game writer Marta Malinowska said during the speech at the Paszporty Polityki Awards:
[i]“This is a game about rage, and about turning it into something good. I want to dedicate it to all the people who took their anger this year, took to the streets, and decided to do something about the surrounding reality.”[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38367964/e12412e894ba291b27fc4f45b9f942349e6175b9.jpg[/img]

During this year, we have been improving the game experience for the PC players - we've released [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1450260/Werewolf_The_Apocalypse__Heart_of_the_Forest__Digital_Goodies_Pack/]a free goodies pack here on Steam[/url], and later on added the support for the Steam badges, backgrounds, trading cards, and emojis.
At the beginning of this year, we've released the game for the console players on Nintendo Switch, Playstation, and Xbox platforms... and maybe in the future, there will come another platform the game could be released on ;)
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38367964/c802c6a7e78d469d0ba8ae34d164ab4d07998d46.jpg[/img]

We're also super happy that after the release of Heart of the Forest so many players got the ability to know more about "Werewolf: The Apocalypse" from the World of Darkness. With the release of "Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood" game, "World of Darkness: Crimson Thaw" comic (did you heard about it? [url=https://www.worldofdarkness.com/news/exclusive-preview-of-the-world-of-darkness-crimson-thaw-1-comic-book]It looks super cool![/url]), and soon the release of fifth edition of the tabletop RPG - we're sure the different flavors of each will make its fans and expand the imagination of another generation around the whole world.

Thank you for playing,
Different Tales and Walkabout Games

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1342620/Werewolf_The_Apocalypse__Heart_of_the_Forest/

notes.title: It took 30+ years to make our dream comic book game.
notes.content:
I'm Robert. I produced Liberated. I first dreamt of making it around 30 years ago and seeing it out feels unreal.

Liberated is a game. It's also a comic book. Let me explain how it started. 
When I was a kid, back in the 80’s, my homeland Poland was a gloomy place. It was an enslaved country ruled by a strange, sad military guy. I guess I escaped into comics. At first, these were rather crude Polish comics: Tytus or Kapitan Żbik. Later came the good stuff, like Expedition and Funky Koval.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34782333/06c67f2f457b90ed5c64e8be6b31cb7b0ebd08f1.jpg[/img]

Soon I was reading everything, from Donald Duck to Punisher, from Thorgal to Batman. This was right after the system changed and suddenly we got access to all kinds of colorful American stories. I was into them so much that I sometimes dreamt about them. 
 
(I shit you not, I still sometimes dream I’m in a comic book store and can’t afford anything - I have had this traumatic dream since childhood!)

Anyway, in one dream, after I watched Tim Burton's Batman, the panels moved like a film. This stuck with me for some time and then I forgot about it.

Years passed and then I saw... Harry Potter. You remember these moving photos from the films?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34782333/05f8524728ca7efdd48aed83a972f1178757820d.gif[/img]

That's when I remembered my moving comic idea. And since by that time I was into gaming, I wished I could make a game like that. But it seemed impossible, not with early 2000s' technology, to create what I had in mind. Not just a game with some comic book elements, but a realistically rendered comic with moving panels. 
 
After all, games back then looked like this:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34782333/b9aaafc4617dc40d1b720b1df68e9e63ca57a6bc.gif[/img]

So I stopped thinking about it.
 
Around 3 years ago I met Marek, who worked on games. We talked and he told me about his idea for a dystopian story-driven game. I noticed it's a bit similar to V for Vendetta, and a lightbulb lit in my head. A comic book with moving panels! Moreover, with panels YOU CONTROL.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34782333/04ba2340be3639fe741378f63b461b46b4a51037.gif[/img]

Over 2.5 years, we poured our soul into making this game. At first, it was supposed to be a pixelart title, but it didn't work, it wasn't what I had in mind.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34782333/eee95468b2b662e4316a0f2f394ad766ccc267fc.gif[/img]


We then switched to a totally hand-drawn 2D game as you can see above. But it was still too simple, it didn't really suit the dystopian themes. We wanted the game to be noir, like Frank Miller's comics.

And so we arrived at a mix of 2D and 3D. I thought it looked JUST RIGHT! It's rendered as a fully realistic comic, you can even see the shine on the pages.
 
Gameplay-wise, it's a side-scrolling action adventure. This genre worked best for the formula. Stages couldn't be too long, controls too complex. We wanted to make the game not only look, but FEEL like a comic.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34782333/f863c771bdc8debc80fb2d8bb329f2b9a84c1ba6.gif[/img]

Today, Liberated is here on PC and Switch, and this feels just unreal. It's literally a dream come true!
 
I'm trying to say that you should never give up on your dreams. Maybe in 30 years, you'll get a chance to make them happen.
 
Thanks for reading!

notes.title: Different Kind of Cyberpunk
notes.content:
[b]When you think cyberpunk, do you just see neon lights and cybernetics? [/b]

Cyberpunk has a rich history of fiction about mass surveillance and control via technology... that's already here. The "high tech, low life" fiction of the 20th century is becoming the reality of the 21st.

So that snazzy outrun aesthetic that we associate with cyberpunk nowadays is certainly one way to do it and keep cyberpunk sci-fi — but it's not the only way to go!

In Liberated, we present you with a different kind of cyberpunk:
A noir cyberpunk.
A grounded cyberpunk.
A [i]look out your window for pete's sake[/i] cyberpunk!

notes.title: Comix Zone vs. Liberated: are they really similar?
notes.content:
Over the past few days we've been debating this a lot as a team: is it fair to call Liberated [i]the first playable comic book[/i]? What about Comix Zone or even Framed, haven't they done this before?

So we decided to write up some of our thoughts and invite you to talk!

[h3]Comix Zone vs. Liberated: are they really similar?[/h3]
[b]Yes.[/b] They're video games that look like comics.
[b]But also not really...[/b]

When we set out to create a [i]playable graphic novel [/i] we knew that we're going all-in on the concept. Not making a game that's like a comic book in one way or another. We started creating a [i]digital comic that you read and play[/i]. 

Even having established this, the Comix Zone comparison is inevitable, Comix Zone is part of our DNA. [b]But is it really similar?[/b]

First things first, Comix Zone is TO THIS DAY absolutely outstanding. It dared to do something incredibly creative with the comic book framework: it made a comic ALIVE. Its wonderful, vigorous art style makes it look great even today. 

[b]It's also what makes Comix Zone so different from Liberated.
[/b]
Comix Zone takes comic book traditions and tropes, both narrative and visual, and then it goes crazy. The protagonist is aware of the fact that he lives inside a comic book. He jumps between panels, breaks the fourth wall--the game is very tongue-in-cheek in this regard. It's like a test of how far you can push interactivity in gaming; how wild your imagination can run. 

For this reason, Comix Zone isn't exactly a playable comic book—because it's not a story told through this medium. It's a super fun and imaginative parody of comics, showing what would happen if some mystical force made these hand-drawn characters come to life.

[b]For Liberated, we wanted something different. We wanted to simulate the paper comic — embrace its boundaries — make you feel like you are interacting with a real comic book. [/b]

We love the smell of paper, the sound of pages turning, the dynamics of framing, the way onomatopoeias stimulate senses they don't actually pertain to. 

And so, Liberated is at its core a comic book story, a graphic novel — like the ones you can find in comic book shops. It just so happens this one is rendered and has panels where you decide what happens through gameplay. But it has a cover, pages you can turn, issues to collect, and it's 'printed' on a glossy paper that reflects light when seen from a certain perspective. It doesn't break through the comic book limitations, it embraces them and lives within them.

[b]To us this is the critical difference between Comix Zone and Liberated.[/b]

[i]Comix Zone is an action game that has fun with comic book aesthetics. [/i]

[i]Liberated is a comic book that you can play.[/i]

[h3]But what do you think?[/h3]

notes.title: We live in a world of hackers
notes.content:
The [i]average time[/i] between hacker attacks on any computer with internet access is [b]39 seconds.[/b]

In a study by the University of Maryland, [i]2,244 attempts[/i] to breach into a single computer were made in one day.


These attacks [b]aren't targeted.[/b]

These attacks [b]aren't manual.[/b]

They're automated and [b]seek out unsecured computers.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34782333/19a4654c147aa9495b1fb9adc8da6766172752d1.jpg[/img]

[b]In 2015, recognizing a data breach took companies an average of 6 months.[/b]

If your data is acquired, it's not immediately used It's usually flagged as promising for future use or not. You can be a victim of hacking and not realize it for a long time.

Consequences can be felt [i]years after the incident.
[/i]
And that's why we consider Liberated to be a fairly grounded game. Every day, there's [i]less and less fiction in science-fiction.[/i]

[b]Welcome to reality![/b]

notes.title: 7 Insurgent Things To Do In Liberated (As Seen On IGN)
notes.content:
The [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wV0uQTE6ubk]new gameplay footage we shared on IGN[/url] shed some light on the true nature of the Liberated’s insurgent activities. Here’s what you can expect when you join the fight, but remember: once you oppose the system, there will be no going back…


[b]1. Pop the red pill[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34782333/7b6005fde81998023b6e89f41417a0a8859a982c.gif[/img]
Getting recruited is a Neo moment (you know, from The Matrix): suddenly, everything around you changes, or at least your perspective does. You peek behind the veil of mainstream reality and discover truths that you are not ready for.



[b]2. Be on the run[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34782333/66997c0324b34d58123909ed5e5deb775ce53665.gif[/img]
There’s surveillance everywhere, and the advanced facial recognition system can make you a target in an instant. The Liberated expect to be hunted, so get ready for high-speed getaways, rooftop chases, marshland pursuits, and more.



[b]3. Make new friends[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34782333/653f132e80a8c0aec2135b95511b87dbed65e102.gif[/img]
The Liberated may seem like an odd bunch, but they’re just ordinary people who can’t stand around with their arms crossed when the world is plunging into madness. Dialogue choices will give you a chance to add a bit of your honest emotions into your interactions with them.



[b]4. Infiltrate government facilities[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34782333/a9537cc730b199997297e7d75b44ba67327bd513.gif[/img]
It’s all about getting where you’re not supposed to. Once you’re there, you will things that would get your a capital punishment if you were captured.



[b]5. Get sneaky[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34782333/6169b9f48eeb10df3cc7d933cd731e90fe3e95ff.gif[/img]
Shadow is your friend, and patience can take you a long way. Hide, wait for an unexpecting enemy to approach, and... Now there's one less enemy to worry about. 



[b]6. Lock and load[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34782333/b055b1d7d1106a0285a3ae71e7a3c4c77683504d.gif[/img]
When things get out of control, or if you just like to go in guns-blazing, hold your breath, aim steadily, and go for a headshot. And remember: you’re doing this for the cause.



[b]7. Expect the unexpected[/b]
Being an insurgent isn’t exactly something you can calculate and predict, so always be prepared for a surprise. You never know when you’re going to have to hack into a federal database or attend a secret meeting. So, are you ready to join the cause?

notes.title: January Dev Blog
notes.content:
[b]Hello everybody! So we're a few weeks into 2020. In just a couple of months Liberated will be out, so everyone is hard at work on the finishing touches... and some pretty big changes.[/b]

[b][i]Here’s what we’ve been up to this month...[/i][/b]

Marek, our [i]Creative Director[/i], and Konrad (that’s me) had a really good chat with [b]NintendoLife[/b]. In the interview, we talk about how Liberated got started, inspirations, challenges, and a lot more. It actually turned out pretty insightful, so [url=https://www.nintendolife.com/news/2020/01/feature_liberated_developer_on_the_challenges_of_creating_a_truly_playable_comic_book][b]check it out here[/b][/url].

[b]As for the game development itself, the final stretch is busy and exciting![/b] We’re doing a lot of playtesting, already two rounds in with more to come. It’s been ridiculously insightful, and we’re making changes and tackling feedback as it comes up.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34782333/9207b2e286938b1488da87dfee1ab68290c3b927.gif[/img]

We’ve actually made tweaks and changes across the board: gameplay, sound, and writing have all been updated!

[b]We’ve implemented tweaks to aiming physics, fixes, and all kinds of improvements to player animations.[/b] So altogether the gameplay feels much smoother now — it’s little things, technically, but they mean so much!

[b]We’re doing a complete audio overhaul[/b], too: updating sound effects, music, and behind-the-scenes performance updates — that last part is especially crucial for the Nintendo Switch version.

And I think the most noticeable change is the [b]all-new writing[/b]. We recently brought Chris on board, an experienced editor who’s worked on projects like Frostpunk, Beat Cop, and Wanderlust Travel Stories. 
We ended up rewriting Every. Single. Line. of dialogue throughout the whole game — aiming for more distinct characters, better dynamics, and that noir comic book feels.

Liberated is still the same game, but we hope it’s a much better one since the last time we showed it off in public. We’re heading to PAX East soon, and damn excited to start showing off what’s new. Keep in touch on [url=https://www.facebook.com/liberatedgame/]Facebook[/url] and [url=https://twitter.com/LiberatedGame]Twitter[/url], our New Year's resolution is to share more shenanigans!

We really want to know what you think as well: what are YOU most hyped about in Liberated? And what are most concerned about? Let’s chat in the comments!

Much love!
[i]-Konrad from the Liberated Team[/i]

notes.title: Watch the first gameplay trailer for Liberated
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34782333/17f1ec82335ac12dafe0864681104b30e1cae947.jpg[/img]

[h1]See the first gameplay trailer for Liberated—a fully playable tech-noir graphic novel; coming soon to PC. Experience how the hand-drawn comic book storytelling seamlessly transitions into fully playable sequences as you fight for what’s right using stealth, wits, and firepower![/h1]

https://youtu.be/pxmQ5lkEn_k

Liberated combines a video game with the experience of reading a comic, transitioning seamlessly—panel by panel—between action, stealth, puzzles, and a hand-drawn story rich in choices.

Liberated is set in the near-future, a tech-noir society slipping into the throes of authoritarianism. Corporate power, state-driven misinformation, government surveillance and weaponized personal data have painted the world in shades of grey where there is no clear right or wrong. In Liberated, truth is relative, revolution is near, and players will experience both sides of this conflict.

[i]”We intend Liberated to be a thought-provoking experience, and we're touching on very real, familiar subjects." [/i]said Marek Czerniak, Creative Director at Atomic Wolf. [i]“Liberated asks difficult questions about modern technology, control over information, and how all that power can enable the rise of authoritarianism."[/i]

[i]"This is the start of our own revolution in digital comics—meaningful interactions, rich gameplay, choices and consequences."[/i] said Robert Purzycki, co-founder of Walkabout.[i] "Our Playable Graphic Novel framework can one day enable creators from game and comic communities to collaborate on their own projects. That's the dream!"[/i]

The SXSW Gaming Pitch Competition Finals featured guest judges Kiki Wolfkill (343 Industries), Raphael Colantonio (Independent), and Nigel Lowrie (Devolver Digital).
